countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

courses.name: B.E./B.Tech in Civil Engineering
courses.summary: A four-year undergraduate engineering degree covering structural analysis and design, geotechnical engineering, transportation engineering, water resources, environmental engineering, surveying and construction management. Programmes pair lecture teaching with materials, hydraulics and surveying laboratories, site visits and a final-year design project. Graduates work in construction, infrastructure, consultancy and public works, or continue to a master's specialisation.

courses.name: B.E./B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering

Graduates move into manufacturing, automotive, energy, thermal and design roles, or continue to a master's specialisation such as thermal engineering or machine design.

universities.name: J.P. College of Engineering

cover.rights: Official institution homepage image used for the college catalogue profile
cover.altText: J.P. College of Engineering main academic building and entrance courtyard in Ayikudi

universities.summary: J.P. College of Engineering is a private, non-autonomous engineering college in Ayikudi, Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu. Founded in 2008, it is affiliated to Anna University, Chennai, and its seven full-time undergraduate engineering branches appear in the AICTE 2026-27 approved-course register. The documented government-quota route is Tamil Nadu Engineering Admissions counselling.
universities.campusLifestyle: The college is at College Road, Ayikudi. Its official library page lists opening hours of 08:00-18:00 on working days and during vacations, a DELNET digital-journal collection, and seven-day borrowing for students. The college also lists an NSS unit and technical symposiums; ask for a current campus visit if facilities matter to your choice.
universities.cityProfile: Ayikudi is in Tenkasi district in southern Tamil Nadu. The TNEA 2026 college booklet places the campus about 5 km from the district headquarters and about 7 km from Tenkasi Junction railway station. Those are the booklet’s reported distances, not door-to-door journey times. Applicants comparing travel or daily commuting should verify their route from the specific hostel or home address.
universities.practicalExposure: J.P. College of Engineering is non-autonomous, so students follow Anna University degree regulations. The Computer Science page names operating systems, data structures, network programming, cloud computing, mobile application development and software engineering laboratories. The AI department names programming, machine-learning, analytics, deep-learning and natural-language-processing labs. Its training and placement cell says it coordinates workshops, career guidance and recruitment; the site does not establish a guaranteed internship or job outcome for any branch.
universities.hostelOverview: The TNEA 2026 booklet lists permanent accommodation for men and women, with a mess for each. It states room rent of ₹2,000 and mess bill of ₹2,000 per annum, plus a ₹1,000 admission fee; these figures are unusually low, so obtain a current written total and confirm what they include. The college hostel page shows separate men’s and women’s facilities and lists security, water and power backup.
universities.dietarySupport: The 2026 TNEA booklet marks both vegetarian and non-vegetarian mess options for the boys’ and girls’ hostels. It does not publish a meal plan or confirm whether both choices are served daily. Ask the hostel office about the current menu and all charges.
universities.safetyOverview: The college’s hostel page lists 24/7 security, and the TNEA booklet publishes an anti-ragging phone number: 8012520500. Those are institutional facilities and contact details; check current hostel supervision and grievance procedures before moving in.
universities.studentSupport: For admission or quota questions, the college lists principal@jpcoe.ac.in and 80125 20500. The placement cell lists placement@jpcoe.ac.in for training and recruitment support. TNEA counselling and certificate questions should be checked against the current government portal, because the 2026 registration window has passed.

faq.question: Is J.P. College of Engineering in Tenkasi a university?
faq.answer: It is a private, non-autonomous engineering college affiliated to Anna University, Chennai. Anna University lists it under Tenkasi with examination code 9512; its TNEA counselling code is 4994.

faq.question: Which engineering degrees does the college currently offer?
faq.answer: AICTE and TNEA 2026-27 records list seven undergraduate branches: AI and Data Science, Civil, Computer Science, Electrical and Electronics, Electronics and Communication, Information Technology, and Mechanical Engineering. No current postgraduate degree appears in the checked AICTE register.

faq.question: How do I apply through Tamil Nadu engineering counselling?
faq.answer: Check the current TNEA brochure, register on its official portal, complete certificate verification, and list J.P. College of Engineering under code 4994 with your chosen branch. The 2026 registration window has passed; use the next published schedule for future applications.

faq.question: Can an applicant from outside India apply?
faq.answer: A general foreign-national route was not verified. The 2026 TNEA brochure permits Tamil Nadu-native OCI/PIO cardholders under specified conditions, while the 2026-27 AICTE special-quota lists show no JPCOE entry. Ask the college for written confirmation before assuming another route is available.

faq.question: What academic marks are needed for TNEA?
faq.answer: The 2026 brochure required a pass in HSC or equivalent and a Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry average of 45% for General Category or 40% for the listed reserved categories. It also provides a separate eligible vocational route; check the next brochure before applying.

faq.question: What is the tuition for a B.E. or B.Tech at this college?
faq.answer: No current branch-specific tuition amount was verified in the college or TNEA sources. The TNEA college booklet says tuition follows Government norms. Request a written academic-year and quota-specific fee schedule before paying or comparing offers.

faq.question: Are hostel rooms available?
faq.answer: The 2026 TNEA college booklet lists permanent boys’ and girls’ accommodation and mess facilities. It quotes ₹2,000 for room rent and ₹2,000 for mess bill per annum, plus a ₹1,000 admission fee; confirm what these figures cover and the current total with the college.

faq.question: Is the college autonomous or NBA accredited?
faq.answer: The TNEA 2026 booklet marks the college non-autonomous and shows no NBA accreditation for any of the seven branches. Its degrees follow Anna University affiliation and its engineering courses appear in the AICTE 2026-27 register.

faq.question: Are the college website intake numbers current?
faq.answer: Use the 2026-27 AICTE register and TNEA 2026 booklet when checking seats. Both list 120 seats each for AI and Data Science and Electronics and Communication, while the college’s programme cards still show 60 for those branches.

items: Pass Class 12 HSC (academic stream) or an accepted equivalent with Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry.

evidence.claimText: J.P. College of Engineering is a private self-financing college at College Road, Ayikudi, Tenkasi, founded in 2008.
AICTE 2026-27 approved-institutions register lists J.P. College of Engineering under permanent ID 1-2819861 and application 1-46268025973.
Anna University CAI lists J P College of Engineering under Tenkasi with examination code 9512 and TNEA code 4994.
AICTE and TNEA 2026-27 list seven current full-time UG engineering branches, with no PG branch in the checked register.
The college has an Ayikudi campus; its library is open 08:00 to 18:00 on working days and vacations.
TNEA 2026 lists permanent boys and girls hostels, a ₹2,000 annual room-rent figure, a ₹2,000 annual mess-bill figure, and a ₹1,000 admission fee; current total needs confirmation.
TNEA 2026 counselling lists J.P. College of Engineering under college code 4994 and applies stated nativity and HSC rules.
JPCOE publishes an anti-ragging contact in the TNEA booklet and separate men’s and women’s hostel accommodation.
The college publishes a training and placement cell with workshops, counselling and campus recruitment coordination; no individual outcome is guaranteed.
